dedupe_keys.name: miraca multimodal transport flow allocation model for europe deliverable 2 4

description: The MIRACA transport flow model allocates freight and passenger flows onto the European multimodal transport network, covering maritime, air, rail, road and inland waterway flows. It works in three steps: it estimates sources and sinks of flows, builds origin-destination matrices, and assigns the flows to the networks, which lets users identify critical lifelines. Inputs are the Eurostat Supply and Use Tables, E-PRTR industrial facilities, GHSL population grids and the TEN-T networks, and the outputs include node and edge flows, inflows and outflows at ports and airports, and corridor flows. It was produced by Fernandez-Perez, Pant and Li in the MIRACA project, funded by Horizon Europe grant 101004174, as Deliverable 2.4. Coverage is continental (Europe). The code is a set of Python Jupyter notebooks, deposited on Zenodo on 30 January 2026 as a 216 MB zip file, free under CC BY 4.0. Caveats: it is a research deliverable, the flows are modelled, not observed, and the results depend on the Eurostat and TEN-T inputs. It supports network flow analysis, criticality ranking of transport links and cascading failure studies across modes. It complements the TEN-T network data catalogued here and is related to the Eurostat transport statistics.
